issue_context.title: "This directory already contains a Godot project" when inputting a valid path without trailing /
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.0.3.stable.official [5222a99f5]

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

Inputting a project path without a trailing / results in a warning:

> This directory already contains a Godot project

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/43559/536fd129-cb2c-4739-ab74-d379afb99034)

It's not obvious that you need to add a trailing slash to fix.

Godot detected there's a project in this folder, so could it add the trailing slash for me? or accept paths without it?

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Godot
2. Click Import
3. Type path to existing project. When you've typed the path (but without the trailing `/`), you'll see the error.

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
comments:
The error message is unclear, but isn't due to the missing slash, but an incorrect check, will make a fix

Unfortunately I'm unable to test it due to #77760, will do some checking though
Oh, I see the slash wasn't required for another project. I guess it's actually because the path ends with "zip". Thanks for figuring that out!

review_comments: Any reason we shouldn't `strip_edges()` here and not have to deal with doing the logic twice with and without stripping below?

That's a good point, will take a look, kept it as original originally, most of the code here does two options, with and without stripping edges

I suspect trailing and leading space might be valid file name parts on some platforms or something

Right, on Linux I can have trailing and leading space:
```
$ file "  LICENSE.txt  " 
  LICENSE.txt  : ASCII text
```

Reordering here in the weird case where there's a file matching but not a directory, unsure if this will ever happen, but it can't hurt, though I'm not even sure trailing and leading spaces are valid for paths in any OS
